package_info.package_manager: proprietary (commercial software, not public package manager)
package_info.package_versions: 2019.4 through 2020.2.1 (as per public reporting, but not specified in this report)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is considered malicious because attackers injected a sophisticated backdoor into the build process, resulting in digitally signed, production-distributed software containing attacker-controlled code. This enabled covert remote access, command execution, and data exfiltration across a wide range of downstream users and organizations, representing a severe supply chain compromise.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the Orion Business Layer Host process starts and runs)
execution_context.file_location: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (compiled and distributed in compromised Orion builds)
required_permissions: environment_vars (to gather system and environment information)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks if it is running within the SolarWinds.BusinessLayerHost process, then periodically initiates outbound HTTP/S connections to hardcoded attacker-controlled C2 domains, receives remote commands, and executes them on the host system, enabling covert remote attacker control and persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code is suspicious because it introduces hidden, unauthorized network communications to external domains and enables remote command execution, which are not part of legitimate Orion software functionality. The code is obfuscated, not present in official source, and is designed to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate SolarWinds Orion software should not contain hidden backdoor logic, should not beacon to undocumented external domains, and should never execute arbitrary remote commands received over the network, especially in production, digitally signed releases.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate remote management or update features may contact central servers, but these are always documented, use official SolarWinds infrastructure, and do not allow arbitrary remote command execution. Such features are visible to administrators and subject to audit.
key_indicators: Outbound HTTP/S connections to hardcoded, non-SolarWinds C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com)
Periodic beaconing behavior from the BusinessLayerHost process
Execution of attacker-supplied commands received from C2
Code sections not present in official source repositories
Persistence and anti-analysis techniques to evade detection

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains unauthorized access to the SolarWinds build infrastructure, typically via credential compromise, insider threat, or exploitation of misconfigurations.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to modify build artifacts and inject malicious code into production software.

attack_chain.action: Malicious backdoor code is injected into the Orion software during the build process, specifically into the SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in digitally signed, production releases distributed to customers.

attack_chain.action: Compromised Orion software is distributed to customers via normal update channels, appearing as legitimate updates.
attack_chain.leads_to: Widespread deployment of backdoored software across customer environments.

attack_chain.action: At runtime, the malicious code within the Orion BusinessLayerHost process beacons to attacker-controlled C2 domains, receives remote commands, and executes them on the victim system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote attacker control, data exfiltration, lateral movement, and further compromise of victim environments.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound HTTP/S connections from SolarWinds Orion servers to external, non-SolarWinds domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com)
Periodic beaconing behavior from the BusinessLayerHost process (SolarWinds.BusinessLayerHost.exe)
Execution of commands or scripts received from remote servers by the Orion process
Presence of obfuscated or anomalous code sections in Orion DLLs
file_indicators: Modified SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with code sections not present in official source or known-good versions
Digitally signed Orion binaries with unexpected or anomalous code blocks
File hashes of Orion DLLs that do not match official releases
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known SolarWinds C2 domains such as avsvmcloud.com, digitalcollege.org, freescanonline.com, deftsecurity.com, and others associated with the campaign
Unusual DNS queries or HTTP/S requests from Orion servers to domains not owned by SolarWinds
Beaconing patterns (regular intervals, specific HTTP headers or URIs) from Orion servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor SolarWinds Orion servers for unexpected outbound network connections to non-SolarWinds domains, especially those linked to known C2 infrastructure. Analyze Orion DLLs (e.g., SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll) for code sections not present in official source or known-good builds, and verify digital signatures and file hashes. Use EDR or AV tools to detect periodic beaconing and remote command execution behavior. Audit build infrastructure for unauthorized changes to build artifacts and monitor for the presence of obfuscated or anomalous code in production binaries.
